questions.q: Which list contains the six habits Burchard found in high performers?
a: Clarity, energy, necessity, productivity, influence and courage
Clarity, discipline, ambition, focus, charisma and resilience
Purpose, passion, optimism, efficiency, networking and boldness
Vision, health, urgency, planning, persuasion and bravery
questions.why: The overview and lessons name seeking clarity, generating energy, raising necessity, increasing productivity, developing influence and demonstrating courage.

a: Having an external reason that pushes you beyond selfish goals
Making every task urgent by setting tight deadlines
Focusing only on work that brings personal fame
Raising your standards until nothing is good enough
questions.why: Lesson 2 says necessity gives you an outside reason for your work, turning attention away from selfish desires for success.

questions.q: How does Burchard suggest increasing productivity?
a: Spend energy only on the work that is truly vital
Answer emails first so your inbox stays clear
Work longer hours to fit in more tasks
Delegate the most important work to others
questions.why: Lesson 2 says to separate important work from unimportant work and direct your energy at what matters.

questions.q: What is the deadline trap, and how does Burchard suggest countering it?
a: Ignoring your own due dates; commit to a date and use a Ulysses Contract
Setting deadlines too early; add extra time to every estimate
Missing other people's deadlines; apologize and renegotiate
Avoiding all deadlines; work until the task feels finished
questions.why: Lesson 2 describes the deadline trap as failing to hold yourself to deadlines and recommends a firm date plus a Ulysses Contract.

questions.q: What do high performers do with their boldest goals, according to the summary?
a: Share them openly even when others call them unrealistic
Keep them private until the work is finished
Announce them only after early results appear
Test them quietly with a small trusted group
questions.why: Lesson 3 says top performers speak openly about big goals even when others dismiss them as fantasy.
